LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO file describes a benign AIMP skin package. The metadata is straightforward: it depends on the AIMP player (`depends = aimp`), needs libarchive to handle the archive type (`makedepends = libarchive`), and has a pinned SHA256 checksum (`sha256sums = f919e405...`). The single source fetches a prebuilt `.archive` file from aimp.ru's official download catalog endpoint (`https://aimp.ru/?do=catalog.download&id=499`), which is the legitimate upstream source for AIMP skins — downloading the package's own declared source from its own project's domain is expected behavior, not a supply-chain risk.

No dangerous constructs are present: there are no `eval`, base64 decoding, `curl|bash` pipelines, reverse shells, credential theft, or attempts to modify unrelated system files. The `&` in the URL is correct XML escaping for the ampersand in the `do=catalog.download` query parameter. Options `!strip` and `!debug` are standard for preserving a binary skin archive. The date-based `pkgver = 20261001` is an unconventional versioning scheme but not malicious. The GitHub URL (`github.com/badcast/aimpskins`) is a plausible upstream/fork tracking page for the skin pack and does not execute any code.

There is no evidence of injected malicious code, data exfiltration, or backdoors. All operations are consistent with ordinary AUR packaging of an AIMP skin archive.
</details>
